questions.prompt: CartService is providedIn: 'root'. A product page also lists it in its component providers. What happens?

options.text: Nothing changes; Angular reuses the root instance
The product page and its children get a second, separate instance, so the rest of the app doesn't see their changes
Angular throws a duplicate provider error
The root instance is destroyed and replaced

questions.explanation: Each injector caches its own instance. A component-level provider creates a new instance for that subtree, which breaks sharing with the rest of the app.

questions.prompt: Match each provider location to what it gives you.

pairs.right: One instance for the whole app
One instance shared by a feature's route subtree
A private instance per component, shared with its children

questions.explanation: Use root for shared state, route providers to scope state to one feature, and component providers for state that must be private to one widget.

questions.prompt: Which belong in a facade's public API? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Read-only computed() selectors like entries and loading
Intent methods like add() and remove(id)
The injected HttpClient so components can make their own calls

questions.explanation: Components should read state through read-only selectors and change it only through intent methods. Writable state and HttpClient stay hidden.

questions.prompt: Order the steps of an optimistic delete inside a facade.

items.text: Remember the entry and its position
Patch state with a new array that leaves the entry out
Call the API to delete it
If the call fails, put the entry back and set an error message

questions.explanation: Save what you need to undo, update the UI immediately, call the server, and roll back on failure.

questions.prompt: Why split a feature into an API service and a facade?

options.text: Angular requires HttpClient to be injected in a separate class
The API service knows endpoints and mapping; the facade knows state and rules, so each stays small and testable

questions.explanation: Separating HTTP from state lets you test the facade with a stubbed API and change endpoints without touching state logic.

questions.prompt: Which signal method returns a read-only view of a writable signal, so other classes can read it but not set it?
questions.explanation: Keep the writable signal private and expose signal.asReadonly() or a computed() selector.
